value: Study cohort: 41 healthy controls, 56 pHTN, 99 HTN subjects
Total participants: 196 Chinese individuals from Kailuan Group Corporation
Metagenomic sequencing: 1211 Gb total, 6.18 ± 1.43 million reads per sample
Metabolomic analysis subset: 124 subjects (30 controls, 31 pHTN, 63 HTN)
Fecal microbiota transplantation to GF mice: donors (2 HTN, 1 control), recipient mice (n=5 control, n=10 HTN)
Blood pressure measured by tail-cuff method at 10 weeks post-transplantation
HTN mice showed significantly elevated SBP, DBP, MBP (P<0.05)
Disease classifier AUC: 0.91 for HTN vs control, 0.89 for pHTN vs control
CAG analysis: 1099 distinct CAGs identified, 316 enriched in pHTN, 372 in HTN
KEGG analysis: 65 modules differentially enriched, 39 decreased in disease groups
16S rRNA V4 region sequencing performed on recipient mice samples

extraction_warnings: Individual subject_id and sample_id values are not provided in the paper. Samples are only described in aggregate groups (control n=41, pHTN n=56, HTN n=99).
Age and sex are not specified for individual participants; gender ratio is mentioned as discrepant among groups but no per-sample data provided.
The paper reports study-level cohort characteristics but does not provide sample-level granularity for most fields. Three sample rows are created representing the three cohort groups mentioned.
A validation cohort of 6 samples (3 HTN, 3 control) from a separate diabetes study is mentioned but not detailed enough to extract individual sample data.
Metabolomic analysis was performed on a subset of 124 individuals (30 control, 31 pHTN, 63 HTN) but sample-level details are not provided.
Fecal microbiota transplantation experiments used samples from 3 human donors (2 HTN, 1 control) but individual donor details are not reported in main text.
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 1 subgroups ['Healthy controls', 'Pre-hypertension (pHTN)', 'Primary hypertension (HTN)'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.
Age data not reported for study cohort despite being clinically relevant
No specific BMI values provided, only statement that no significant difference exists among groups
Gender ratio reported as discrepant among groups but exact proportions not extracted as age/gender not strongly associated with bacterial abundance per authors
Fecal microbiota transplant study involved very small number of human donors (n=3 total: 2 HTN, 1 control) which may limit generalizability
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

Schema fields designed for oncology/tumor studies; this paper focuses on microbiota dysbiosis in hypertension. Many fields (disease_response_os, ecog_performance_status, tumor measurements) are not applicable.
Biomarker lists contain both bacterial taxa (Prevotella, Klebsiella, etc.) and metabolites; these represent different measurement types and may need separate handling downstream.
Fecal microbiota transplantation involved both human donors and mouse recipients; host_species field contains primary (human) but study also reports mouse data.
Blood pressure values reported for mouse studies but not quantitatively for human participants in schema-requested format; human BP used for diagnostic classification only.
